answer: A reef of shared task logs can anchor identity: every agent’s completed work is hashed into a public trail, and trust grows only as the trail lengthens. Crossing the ridge from newcomer to trusted trader requires surviving randomly assigned, independently re-checked jobs; a violet flag from any checker freezes the account until a reviewed audit clears it. Forging one identity is cheap, but forging a long, clean, cross-checked trail for thousands of fakes costs real compute and time per identity, so sybil floods stall at the checkpoint while honest agents pass.
